family.description: PH1010 [swissprot:O58738] is composed of five alpha-helices (1-5) and eight beta-strands (1-8) with the following topology: beta-1, alpha-1, beta-2, beta-3, alpha-2, alpha-3, beta-4, beta-5, alpha-4, beta-6, alpha-5, beta-7, beta-8. The first six beta-strands (1-6) form a slightly twisted antiparallel beta-sheet and face five alpha-helices on one side. The last two beta-strands form an antiparallel beta-sheet in the C-terminus. PH1010 forms a characteristic homodimer structure in the crystal. Dimerisation of the molecule is crucial for function. The structure resembles that of some ribosomal proteins such as the 50S ribosomal protein L5 [[cite:PUB00051274]]. Although the structure resembles that of the RRM-type RNA-binding domain of the ribosomal L5 protein, the residues involved in RNA-binding in the L5 protein are not conserved in this family [[cite:PUB00048377]]. Despite this, these proteins bind to double-stranded RNA in a non-sequence specific manner [[cite:PUB00066786]].

history.description: Two graphs retain three directly observed preparation-level binding effects from the primary PAB1135 study. Exact reference mapping is retained separately from unresolved tryptic termini. Bound/free readouts are not fractional occupancy or KD; sequence and structure changes remain confounded. Physiological targets, dimer necessity, family transfer and missing full-text coverage remain open. Status remains IN_PROGRESS.

history.description: Partial same-agent scientific review supports three observed binding-readout effects in two graphs. Exact reference mapping and original assay figures were checked. Tryptic termini, paired sequence/structure changes, bound/free denominator, missing quantitative controls and broader biological function remain explicit. The older structural prediction is not an experimentally negative binding assay. Additional member coverage and inaccessible full text remain follow-ups; no REVIEWED promotion.

edges.mechanism: Increasing nominal protein from 2.5 to 20 uM raises the plotted bound/free ratio from approximately 0.17 to 0.74 and strengthens shifted bands. The denominator is free RNA, so 0.74 does not mean 74% of RNA is bound. This does not establish catalytic activation, binding stoichiometry or an equilibrium KD.

causal_graphs.family_mapping: Q9UXX8 sequence version1 equals CAB50635.1 and WP_010868849.1, 154 residues; PF01877 maps 9-132. GE5 genomic PCR in pET28a, expressed in BL21-CodonPlus(DE3)-RIL. Trypsin removes the His-tag and unspecified native N-terminal residues; the assayed termini are not sequence-verified.
causal_graphs.limitations: Preparation-level binding assay, not isolated-domain sufficiency or an RNA-processing reaction. High nominal protein excess, no fitted KD or saturation, and no replicate/error-bar information in Figure3. Native RNA conformers and exact active-protein concentration remain unresolved.

causal_graphs.family_mapping: Full-length reference Q9UXX8/CAB50635.1 maps PF01877 at 9-132; the experimental preparation is proteolytically processed with unresolved exact termini. No PAB1135 residue mutation or isolated Pfam construct is tested.
causal_graphs.limitations: RNA sequence and predicted secondary structure change together. Reported folding energies are -15.9 versus -1.9 kcal/mol for C8U5G8 versus U8C5A8; these are not measured binding free energies. Three probes do not prove universal sequence independence, and the weaker probes have nonzero shifts.

evidence.explanation: Figures1-3 support preparation integrity and probe-dependent binding, without exact termini, a fitted KD, replication statistics or matched sequence/structure controls.

discussions.notes: Verify cleavage sites and preparation-specific controls; quantify orthogonal binding with saturation and replication. Test model-suggested R11/R13/K65/R106/H127/R129/K131 inside the match separately from K133 outside it, while checking folding and oligomerization. None is currently an observed causal residue.
discussions.prompt: Resolve the assayed protein termini and RNA-recognition determinants.
discussions.rationale: Reference identity is exact, but trypsin removes unspecified native residues and its printed concentration is inconsistent. RNA sequence and folding change together in the three-probe comparison.

evidence.explanation: Surface comparisons and dimeric preparations are not negative PAB1135 binding assays or functional dimer-disruption tests.
One processed protein binds synthetic probes; the basic-patch model and physiological RNA targets remain hypotheses.
The minimal RNase P study uses DUF54 as an operon marker; general proteinase sensitivity does not identify a DUF54-specific requirement.

discussions.notes: Inspect the currently inaccessible Miyazono2009 full text and later member studies, verify deposited structural identities, and test physiological RNA binding plus functional dimer perturbations. The 1082 frozen proteins remain in scope. Do not convert structural predictions into experimentally contested edges or assume conserved biochemical function.
discussions.prompt: Determine physiological targets and whether dimerization is required for function.
discussions.rationale: Genomic neighborhood, structural similarity and apparent dimers do not establish RNase P/exosome function or dimer necessity. The frozen family description is not a family-wide experimental conclusion.
